title: Everyone Drives the Qinghai-Gansu Loop in 7 Days — Too Fast | China Travel Expert
description:
The Qinghai-Gansu grand loop is about 2,800 km of northwest China in one ring — and most people blitz it in 7 days. I'd give it nine.

The loop strings together salt lakes, desert, grassland and Silk Road towns: Qinghai Lake, the sky-mirror of Chaka Salt Lake, the rainbow hills of Zhangye Danxia, the singing dunes and Crescent Lake at Dunhuang, and the Great Wall's end at Jiayuguan. Done in a week, that's roughly five hours behind the wheel every day — you end up seeing the best of it through a windscreen. Add a day or two, especially a full day at Dunhuang for the Mogao Caves and Mingsha dunes, and the same route turns from a checklist into a trip.

🧭 Expert Tip: book Mogao Caves online about a month ahead — entries are capped and sell out — and build in buffer days for weather on the high passes. Reconfirm distances and opening times before you go.

青甘大环线约2800公里，多数人7天刷完——每天开车约5小时。加两天，尤其敦煌留一整天看莫高窟和鸣沙山，这条线才算真正走到。

AI/stock disclosure: narration-free; English subtitles + royalty-free music. This is a route/MAP-format piece: the stops are named as verified route facts, and the b-roll is illustrative licensed Pexels stock of Chinese northwest landscapes (Zhangye Danxia plus Chinese desert/plateau scenery, Ken-Burns stills) — it sets the scene, and not every clip is the exact stop named. Distances and driving times are the commonly published figures for the standard loop; reconfirm before you travel.
